memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You shall not commit adultery. - Deut 5:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God protects marriage with this command because marriage is one of His most beautiful gifts — a covenant of faithful love between husband and wife. Adultery shatters that covenant. It breaks trust, wounds families, and treats a sacred promise as though it were disposable. God cares deeply about faithfulness, because faithfulness reflects His own unchanging character.

Once again, Jesus takes us beneath the surface. He taught that even a lustful look cherished in the heart is a betrayal of this command (Matt 5:27-28). In a world flooded with images and easy temptation, this is a searching word. Purity is not only about what we do with our bodies but what we feed in our minds and hearts. God calls His people to faithfulness that begins on the inside.

Behind this command stands a wonderful truth: God Himself is the perfectly faithful Bridegroom. Scripture pictures Christ as the Husband who loves His bride, the Church, with a love that never wanders (Eph 5:25-27). His faithfulness to us — even when we are unfaithful — is the foundation and the power for our faithfulness to one another. If you have failed here, His grace is real and cleansing. And His Spirit gives strength to guard your heart, your eyes, and your commitments. Faithfulness is possible because He is faithful.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I guarding not only my actions but my thoughts and desires?
- How does Christ's faithful love for me strengthen my own faithfulness?
- What practical steps can I take to protect purity in my heart and life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the faithful One, and Your love never wanders. Guard my heart, my eyes, and my commitments, and by Your Spirit help me to reflect Your faithfulness in all my relationships. Amen.
